title: Folio Accounting Basis for Resort Lodging Stay Charges
content:
This basis governs how the charges of a Resort Lodging stay reach the folio. Most of its clauses have been superseded by the current bases on which the room rate, the resort charge, the departure services charge and the amount retained on an early departure are worked out, and those clauses are no longer in force. They are carried here in their retired form so that the record of the basis is complete and no reader applies them.

## Clauses no longer in force

1. That the room rate is posted night by night rather than as one figure for the stay, because a stay that straddles two rate windows is priced on the window each night falls in, is no longer in force.
2. That a night falling inside the published holiday window takes the holiday rate, a night inside the peak window takes the peak rate, and every other night takes the base rate, the window being judged on the night occupied and never on the arrival date, is no longer in force.
3. That guests beyond the unit type's standard occupancy add the extra person charge to each night they stay is no longer in force.
4. That the nightly resort charge is posted for every night occupied and is not reduced by any discount, because it pays for services the party has whether or not they use them, is no longer in force.
5. That the housekeeping charge is posted once on departure and the parking charge nightly for spaces beyond those included is no longer in force.
6. That a night the party leaves early is still charged where the departure falls inside the cancellation terms of the stay is no longer in force.

## The clause in force

The resort charge is posted only while the reservation stands as checked in or as checked out, and the standing is read off the collective's own reservation record before the charge is posted.

### Applying the clause in force (hypothetical standings)

A reservation on which the party has arrived and taken keys stands as checked in, so the resort charge may be posted against it. A reservation on which the party has left and the folio has been presented stands as checked out, so the resort charge may still be posted against it. A reservation that is merely firm, with the party not yet arrived, stands in neither of those two, and no resort charge is posted against it while it does so.
